correctness.rationale: Kapranov's Proposition 1.2.4 identifies each Grassmannian torus-orbit closure as a projective normal toric variety with its matroid polytope, and the generic matroid polytope is \(\Delta(k,n)\). The toric degree is the normalized volume, classically \(A(n-1,k-1)\). The torus-orbit decomposition has one orbit per face; positive-dimensional tori have Euler characteristic zero, so \(\chi\) is the number of vertices \(\binom nk\). The comparison is proved for all parameters by a direct Eulerian recurrence lower bound and an elementary parity-class bound for the central binomial coefficient. The package checker independently reconstructs the Eulerian rows and tests every pair through \(n=120\).

value.rationale: Generic torus orbit closures are canonical toric subvarieties of Pluecker Grassmannians and hypersimplices are among the most basic matroid polytopes. Projective degree measures normalized hypersimplex volume while Euler characteristic counts torus fixed points, so the theorem compares two intrinsic geometric complexities of exactly the same family. The result gives a complete phase diagram, identifies dimension four as the sharp onset of interior degree domination, and proves that equality never occurs.
